title: ED fall documentation

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports asking about the details of a fall when a covered person presents after one and explicitly rejects automatic prediction-tool use.
user_facing_items.population: People aged 65 years and over, and people aged 50 to 64 with one or more factors increasing fall risk.
user_facing_items.setting: Community settings including emergency departments and minor injury units, and hospital inpatient settings.
user_facing_items.jurisdiction: England and Wales; requires UAE pathway adaptation
restrictions: Exact for asking details of a fall and for comprehensive clinician assessment of specified falls-risk domains in the covered age group. It does not cover every traumatic injury, younger adults or children, and it must not auto-score fall risk.
user_facing_items.rationale: The exact NICE section supports documenting the details, onset or duration and circumstances of a fall in the covered older/higher-risk population; it does not apply a risk score or cover every age.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports clinician assessment of cardiovascular, cognition, delirium, diet/fluid, dizziness, footwear, function, gait/balance, hearing, long-term conditions, medicines, neurological, osteoporosis, continence and vision domains when relevant
user_facing_items.population: People aged 65 years and over, and people aged 50 to 64 with one or more factors increasing fall risk.

user_facing_items.rationale: The exact comprehensive-assessment section supports documenting functional impact, measured vital data, focused assessment, general appearance and relevant time-critical abnormalities only when clinician-assessed in the covered population.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports signs and symptoms, allergies, medicines, past history, last intake, events or mechanism, examination, interventions, reassessment, and disposition documentation.
user_facing_items.population: Adults and children with acute illness or injury presenting to first-contact emergency care.
user_facing_items.setting: First-contact emergency units and resource-limited emergency-care settings.
restrictions: Exact for structured trauma history, secondary survey, extremity perfusion, and open-wound assessment; partial for minor outpatient injury follow-up, imaging, closure, antibiotics, and UAE pathways.
user_facing_items.rationale: The exact WHO/ICRC trauma history supports recording mechanism, assessed injury severity, examination, existing results and clinician-decided disposition for a traumatic fall without diagnosing an injury.
